messages:
Lina (CS): @here AcmeRetail just escalated — they ran identical rerank payloads against our endpoint before/after last night's rollout and are seeing consistent score shifts and a few top-1 flips. They included two JSON samples. They claim the only change was the model update we rolled at 02:13 UTC.
Ben (Support): Ticket INC-4512 created and ACKed. Customer attached both responses and a quick diff. No 5xx in their app logs. p95 latency increased ~60ms after the deploy.
Lina (CS): Pasting sanitized sample payload + responses from customer (BEFORE = v2.1.0, AFTER = v2.2.0):
```json
{
  "query": "how do I reset my password",
  "candidates": [
    "Click " + "Reset password link in settings",
    "Go to account settings -> security -> reset",
    "Contact support to reset your password",
    "Use the Forgot Password flow on the login page"
  ]
}
```
BEFORE (v2.1.0) response (customer):
```text
[0] "Use the Forgot Password flow on the login page" score=0.87
[1] "Click Reset password link in settings" score=0.72
[2] "Go to account settings -> security -> reset" score=0.64
[3] "Contact support to reset your password" score=0.41
```
AFTER (v2.2.0) response (customer):
```text
[0] "Click Reset password link in settings" score=0.78
[1] "Use the Forgot Password flow on the login page" score=0.74
[2] "Go to account settings -> security -> reset" score=0.66
[3] "Contact support to reset your password" score=0.39
```
Ben (Support): They claim the inputs are byte-for-byte identical. They pinned the model by name but might not have pinned the exact build id. No auth/billing issues reported. They used the hosted rerank route `/v1/rerank`.
Raj (Eng-ML): Thanks. A couple hypotheses: (1) model checkpoint drift (we swapped weights or params between v2.1.0 and v2.2.0), (2) tokenization/normalization change (extra trimming/lowercasing), or (3) runtime quantization/fastpath changed scoring stable behavior. Need deterministic repro with exact model commit sha and deterministic infer settings.
Maya (Eng-Runtime): Can you confirm they used the same `model_version` header? If they omitted an explicit version, routing might have picked a variant with kernel-level quantization enabled. Also checking: any request-level flags like `normalize_whitespace` toggled client-side?
Lina (CS): Customer says they passed `model: "redwood/rerank-small"` and did not specify `model_version`. They expected stable minor patch. I asked them to run again with `?model_version=v2.1.0` vs `?model_version=v2.2.0` and share hashes. Waiting on their follow-up.
Raj (Eng-ML): Meanwhile I'll run quick local harness to call both versions with the exact payload. Use deterministic scoring (greedy) and set seed for the rerank transform. If we reproduce, we can diff the logits/tokenization. Also check tokenizer normalization rules between tags.
Maya (Eng-Runtime): Repro steps for team (run in staging):
```bash
# run against specific model versions
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/rerank-small","model_version":"v2.2.0","queries":[{"query":"how do I reset my password","candidates":["Use the Forgot Password flow on the login page","Click Reset password link in settings","Go to account settings -> security -> reset","Contact support to reset your password"]}]}'
```
Add `model_version=v2.1.0` to test the other.
Raj (Eng-ML): Ran both locally against pinned builds. Preliminary result: I get the same flip between v2.1.0 and v2.2.0. Looking at tokenizer token counts: v2.1.0 tokenized candidate[0] as 5 tokens, v2.2.0 tokenized it as 6 tokens — suggests a normalization/token-split change.
Maya (Eng-Runtime): Deploy bot shows the deploy window for v2.2.0 at 2026-03-02T02:13:14Z with feature flag `fast-tokenize=true` enabled for the rerank family. That flag toggles a new whitespace normalization that can alter token boundaries.
deploy-bot: deploy redwood/rerank-small@v2.2.0 completed by release-ci at 2026-03-02T02:13:14Z
Raj (Eng-ML): If `fast-tokenize` changed tokenization, logits will change and rerank ordering can flip — expected but unfortunate for backward compatibility. We should confirm whether the change was intentional for this minor patch.
Ben (Support): Customer asked for rollback or pin guidance. Suggested workaround: pin `model_version=v2.1.0` until we provide compatibility notes. They're asking for a formal explanation and remediation plan.
Maya (Eng-Runtime): Action plan:
- I'll run a tokenization diff job across our rerank test set and quantify fraction of inputs with tokenization differences.
- If it exceeds threshold, we can consider toggling `fast-tokenize` off for hosted until we do a controlled rollout with explicit release notes.
Raj (Eng-ML): I'll compute score deltas distribution and sample queries with flips. Also produce deterministic artifacts (token lists, logits) for customer repro.
Ben (Support): I'll collect 50 more matched before/after pairs from the customer and upload to S3 (link shared in ticket). I'll also advise them to pin `model_version` in prod.
Lina (CS): I'll update the customer mid-day: we reproduced, likely cause is `fast-tokenize` normalization change — providing pinning workaround and ETA for root-cause doc.
monitoring-bot: Note: rerank p95 latency for prod route increased from 210ms -> 275ms around deploy time; no error-rate spike.
Maya (Eng-Runtime): Quick temporary mitigation: enable `compat-tokenize=true` for routes serving long-standing customers for 48h while we triage.
Raj (Eng-ML): Long term: we should add a release checklist for tokenization/normalization changes that includes a stability eval (rerank/regression) on pinned customer workloads.
Lina (CS): Thanks team. Ben/ Raj/ Maya — keep updates in the ticket INC-4512. I'll pass the workaround to AcmeRetail now. :thumbsup:
